text: Bovine babesiosis is a tick-borne fever caused by the protozoan parasite Babesia (two types identified in Cambodia: Bigemina and Bovis). Signs vary by age, species, and strain; most cases occur in adult cattle, while animals under 9 months are usually symptom-free. Common signs: high fever (up to about 41.5°C) for several days, loss of appetite, the rumen stopping its normal contractions, and clear reluctance to move; conjunctiva starts reddened, then turns pale, then yellow over a few days; urine turns dark red to brown with stable froth; and nervous signs like incoordination and teeth grinding can appear. Treatment: Berenil, given by deep intramuscular injection at 3.5 mg/kg.
